artboards.title: Describe — what do you want to analyse?
Build — a value that needs you
Pipeline file — every value and its reason

annotations.text:
Reached from: the logo, signing in.
Answers “what needs me, what is running, what went wrong” before listing anything. The table’s bar is every value in a pipeline by how it was decided — settled spends no colour.

Reached from: New analysis, the search box, the first visit.
The model turns the sentence into a goal; the person sees and corrects what was understood before anything is built. Strandedness is not guessed. Two ways on: step by step, or all at once.

The step line on the right is the same metro drawing as a route in Code: settled stops are plain, measured ones amber, the current one blue. The proposed step is drawn dashed on the canvas and is not added until the person says so.

An open value is a question with every legal answer listed. The person answers with a reason, which is saved beside the value, or adds a step that measures it instead. Learn it in Code sits under the question it explains.
The second view of the canvas is the file itself. Settings are grouped by step; each shows how it was decided and why. The file on the right is what you download.
Reached from: Run. Three things to confirm, the measured read length shown per sample, and the three places a pipeline can go — only this machine is launched for you.
Built for hundreds of runs: saved views, filters with counts, a dense table. Reserved vs used memory per run shows where compute is wasted; a run that has not finished shows a hatch, not a zero.
Four panels, then the timeline (tasks per step, CPUs asked vs used — used is derived, so hatched), then steps and tasks. Progress is counted in steps, because tasks have no known total.
Dark mode. The failure panel shows the record and nothing interpreted: exit 137 is SIGKILL, and the attempts show each asked and peak memory. Nextflow’s own report is quoted, not explained.
The flow is drawn as a line: found → drafted → with the model → ready for review → in the registry. Only the review stop is red, because only it needs a person.
Grouped by state, with saved views, filters, bulk actions and a detail pane — the same triage pattern as Code’s Requests.
Model answers first and amber, each with the evidence it came from and how many answers it chose among. Checks and the decision on the right; the chat is marked as going to the model.

Comeni Labs — redesigned in the hybrid identity shared with Comeni Code (Lexend, Geist Mono, one meaning per colour, metro lines).

Top bar: logo (home) · Build · Runs · Registry · search that also takes a description · Learn in Code · help · lab.

The loop is describe → build → run → watch. Every board is light except the failed run, which shows dark.
